newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dow boosts Eurobourses, Frankfurt hits peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dow boosts Eurobourses, Frankfurt hits peak.

text.p: Wall Street's bull run, marked by a sixth consecutive record close overnight, boosted European bourses on Thursday and helped leading German shares to new peaks.

On the currency markets the dollar was steady against the mark but firmed against the yen after Japan's "Mr Yen", senior finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara, welcomed a rising dollar and said Tokyo's foreign exchange policy had not changed.

New York's performance gave an early impetus to European equities. The Dow Jones industrial average closed up 8.20 points at 6,274.24 after the Federal Reserve decided to keep U.S. interest rates unchanged. The Dow has surged 245 points, or four percent, since the start of the month

In Frankfurt leading German shares opened bourse trade at record high of 2,785.16, boosted by gains in banking sector, though they later dropped back somewhat. Earlier the IBIS-DAX index of electronic dealings also opened at a new peak.
Major share movers were Commerzbank, up over five percent on continuing merger speculation, and Deutsche Bank and Dresdner Bank also up on higher volumes.
British shares too opened higher but reversed their early gain and continued to lose ground in the late-morning after further evidence of inflationary pressures in the UK.
Stronger-than-expected October retail price data took the steam out of an opening rally, dragging shares and government stocks lower as concerns about another rise in interest rates took a grip.
The figures, described by one economist as "truly awful", wiped out a 13.4 point gain and sent leading shares 13.0 points lower to 3,913.9.

Comments by finance minister Kenneth Clarke that policy would be set to meet the government's 2.5 percent target for underlying inflation reinforced the worries that rates would have to go up again ahead of the next election.

"The mood the market has got itself into about interest rates, we're going to see a continuation of the jitters. If there wasn't an election coming up, rates would probably be higher than they are," said Panmure strategist Ian Williams.

The Paris bourse also opened up, lifted by Wall Street, and later pared some of its gains. The spotlight was on insurer Axa and its rival UAP as the two requoted for the first time since announcing their merger on Monday. As expected, UAP soared at the open, rising 17 percent. Axa shares opened 2.21 percent lower.
On the foreign exchange front the dollar was seen well supported after U.S. Treasury Undersecretary Jeffrey Shafer said on Wednesday the U.S exchange rate policy had not changed.
"Our policy is to have a strong dollar," he said.

Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank America, commented: "Shafer's comments were some of the first indications we have seen of what U.S. policy is under the new Clinton administration. To that extent it provided an important boost for the dollar."

One focus of interest was the seemingly inexorable rise of the pound sterling, which was given a boost by the higher-than- expected UK inflation figures -- seen as a possible precursor to further British rate rises.

The pound had risen sharply on Wednesday after an unexpectedly large decline in UK jobless fuelled expectations of further rate rises. On Thursday it was trading at a fresh four-year high against the dollar of $1.6650. Traders said they saw $1.67 as the next psychological target.
CURRENCIES AT 1115 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5058 marks and 111.66 yen compared with 1.5041 marks and 111.38 yen late in Europe on Wednesday. The (pound was at $1.6650.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1115 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 13.0 at 3,913.9.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was up 2.09 at 2,219.28.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 2.06 at 2,775.66.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $382.65 compared with $384.05 an ounce at the London close on Wednesday. Silver was two cents easier at $4.90. ($1=.6054 Pound)
